translations.literal: Xiaozong took the twenty-second day of the tenth month as the Huiqing Festival; Guangzong took the fourth day of the ninth month as the Chongming Festival; Ningzong took the nineteenth day of the tenth month as the Tianyou Festival, soon changed to the Ruiqing Festival; Lizong took the fifth day of the first month as the Tianji Festival; Duzong took the ninth day of the fourth month as the Qianhui Festival; the Lord of Ying took the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month as the Tianrui Festival.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong’s birthday was observed on the twenty-second day of the tenth month as the Huiqing Festival; Guangzong’s on the fourth day of the ninth month as the Chongming Festival; Ningzong’s on the nineteenth day of the tenth month as the Tianyou Festival, soon renamed the Ruiqing Festival; Lizong’s on the fifth day of the first month as the Tianji Festival; Duzong’s on the ninth day of the fourth month as the Qianhui Festival; and the Lord of Ying’s on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month as the Tianrui Festival.

sentences.zh: 其上壽稱賀之禮，大略皆如天申節儀。

translations.literal: The ceremonies of offering congratulations and birthday wishes were in general all like those of the Tianshen Festival.
translations.idiomatic: The birthday congratulations and celebratory rites were in general the same as those for the Tianshen Festival.

sentences.zh: 諸慶節，古無是也，真宗以後始有之。

translations.literal: The various celebratory holidays did not exist in antiquity; they began only after Zhenzong.
translations.idiomatic: The various celebratory holidays did not exist in antiquity; they began only after Zhenzong.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年，詔以正月三日天書降日為天慶節，休假五日，兩京諸路州、府、軍、監前七日建道場設醮，斷屠宰；

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, an edict established the day on which the Heavenly Writ descended, the third day of the first month, as the Tianqing Festival, with five days of leave; in the two capitals and all circuits, prefectures, armies, and supervisory posts ritual grounds were established and offerings performed for seven days beforehand, and slaughter was forbidden;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1008), an edict established the day on which the Heavenly Writ descended, the third day of the first month, as the Tianqing Festival, with five days of leave. In the two capitals and all circuits, prefectures, armies, and supervisory posts ritual grounds were established and offerings performed for seven days beforehand, and slaughter was forbidden;

sentences.zh: 節日， 士庶特令宴樂，京師然燈。

translations.literal: On the festival day commoners and gentry were specially permitted feasting and music, and lamps were lit in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the festival day commoners and gentry were specially permitted feasting and music, and lamps were lit in the capital.

sentences.zh: 又以六月六日為天貺節，京師斷屠宰，百官行香上清宮。

translations.literal: The sixth day of the sixth month was also made the Tiankuang Festival; in the capital slaughter was forbidden and the hundred officials offered incense at the Palace of Supreme Clarity.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth day of the sixth month was also made the Tiankuang Festival. In the capital slaughter was forbidden and all officials offered incense at the Palace of Supreme Clarity.

sentences.zh: 又以七月一日聖祖降日為先天節，十月二十四日降延恩殿日為降聖節，休假、宴 樂並如天慶節。

translations.literal: The first day of the seventh month, the day the Sacred Ancestor descended, was also made the Xiantian Festival; the twenty-fourth day of the tenth month, the day of descent at the Hall of Extended Grace, was made the Jiangsheng Festival; leave and feasting with music were the same as for the Tianqing Festival.
translations.idiomatic: The first day of the seventh month, the day the Sacred Ancestor descended, was also made the Xiantian Festival, and the twenty-fourth day of the tenth month, the day of descent at the Hall of Extended Grace, was made the Jiangsheng Festival. Leave and feasting with music were the same as for the Tianqing Festival.

sentences.zh: 中書、親王、節度、樞密、三司以下至駙馬都尉，詣長春殿進金縷延壽帶、金絲續命縷，上保生壽酒。

translations.literal: The Secretariat, princes, military commissioners, Bureau of Military Affairs, Three Departments, and those down to commandants of imperial sons-in-law went to the Hall of Eternal Spring to present gold-thread longevity belts and gold-thread life-prolonging cords and to offer life-preserving birthday wine.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat, princes, military commissioners, Bureau of Military Affairs, Three Departments, and those down to commandants of imperial sons-in-law went to the Hall of Eternal Spring to present gold-thread longevity belts and gold-thread life-prolonging cords and to offer life-preserving birthday wine.

sentences.zh: 改禦崇德殿，賜百官飲，如聖節儀。

translations.literal: The venue was changed to the Hall of Reverence for Virtue, where drink was bestowed on the hundred officials, as in the imperial birthday festival ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The venue was changed to the Hall of Reverence for Virtue, where drink was bestowed on all officials, as in the imperial birthday festival ceremony.

sentences.zh: 前一日， 以金縷延壽帶、金塗銀結續命縷、緋彩羅延壽帶、彩絲續命縷分賜百官，節日戴以入。

translations.literal: On the day before, gold-thread longevity belts, gold-plated silver-knotted life-prolonging cords, crimson silk longevity belts, and colored-silk life-prolonging cords were distributed to the hundred officials, who wore them when entering on the festival day.
translations.idiomatic: On the day before, gold-thread longevity belts, gold-plated silver-knotted life-prolonging cords, crimson silk longevity belts, and colored-silk life-prolonging cords were distributed to all officials, who wore them when entering on the festival day.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，宴百官於錫慶院。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished the hundred officials were banqueted at the Court of Bestowed Celebration.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished all officials were banqueted at the Court of Bestowed Celebration.

sentences.zh: 天禧初，詔以大中祥符元年四月一日天書再降內中功 德閣為天禎節，一如天貺節。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxi, an edict established the day on which the Heavenly Writ descended again within the palace at the Merit and Virtue Pavilion on the first day of the fourth month in the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu as the Tianzhen Festival, exactly like the Tiankuang Festival.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianxi, an edict established the day on which the Heavenly Writ descended again within the palace at the Merit and Virtue Pavilion on the first day of the fourth month in the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu as the Tianzhen Festival, exactly like the Tiankuang Festival.

sentences.zh: 尋以仁宗嫌名，改為天祺節。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, because of the taboo name of Renzong, it was changed to the Tianqi Festival.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, because of the taboo name of Renzong, it was changed to the Tianqi Festival.

sentences.zh: 政和三年十一月五日，以修祀事，天真示見，詔為天應節。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the eleventh month in the third year of Zhenghe, because of repair of sacrificial affairs the Heavenly Truth manifested, and an edict established it as the Tianying Festival.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the eleventh month in the third year of Zhenghe (1113), because of repair of sacrificial affairs the Heavenly Truth manifested, and an edict established it as the Tianying Festival.

sentences.zh: 又以五月十二日祭方丘日為寧貺節，既又以二月十五日太上混元上德皇帝降聖日為真元節，八月九日青華帝君生辰為元成節，正月四日有太祖神禦之州府宮殿行香為開基節，十月二十五日為天符節，皆如天慶節，著為令。

translations.literal: The twelfth day of the fifth month, the day of sacrifice at the square mound altar, was also made the Ningkuang Festival; next the fifteenth day of the second month, the day the Supreme Emperor of Mixed Origin and Upper Virtue descended, was made the Zhenyuan Festival; the ninth day of the eighth month, the birthday of the Azure Flower Sovereign Lord, was made the Yuancheng Festival; the fourth day of the first month, when incense was offered at prefectural palaces housing Taizu’s spirit tablet, was made the Kaiji Festival; the twenty-fifth day of the tenth month was made the Tianfu Festival—all like the Tianqing Festival and entered into statute.
translations.idiomatic: The twelfth day of the fifth month, the day of sacrifice at the square mound altar, was also made the Ningkuang Festival. Next the fifteenth day of the second month, the day the Supreme Emperor of Mixed Origin and Upper Virtue descended, was made the Zhenyuan Festival; the ninth day of the eighth month, the birthday of the Azure Flower Sovereign Lord, was made the Yuancheng Festival; the fourth day of the first month, when incense was offered at prefectural palaces housing Taizu’s spirit tablet, was made the Kaiji Festival; and the twenty-fifth day of the tenth month was made the Tianfu Festival—all like the Tianqing Festival and entered into statute.

sentences.zh: 高宗建炎元年十一月五日，詔：“政和以來添置諸節，除開基節外，餘並依祖宗法。”

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the eleventh month in the first year of Jianyan, Gaozong edicted: "The various holidays added since the Zhenghe period, except the Kaiji Festival, shall all follow the ancestral regulations.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the eleventh month in the first year of Jianyan (1127), Gaozong edicted: “The various holidays added since the Zhenghe period, except the Kaiji Festival, shall all follow the ancestral regulations.
